macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Nasdaq and S&P 500 pressured by AI-stock sell-off
items.summary: The Nasdaq and S&P 500 were lower Friday and headed for weekly losses as semiconductor and other AI-related shares remained under pressure. Dow futures were modestly higher, while Thursday’s session ended with the Dow up 1.1%, the S&P 500 up 0.3%, and the Nasdaq up 0.1%.[1][5]

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh gives no signal on upcoming rate decision
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said he would not prejudge upcoming policy meetings, maintaining uncertainty over whether rates will remain unchanged or rise later this month or in early December. Markets priced a 13% probability of a hike at the late-October meeting, down from 28% the previous day.[1][4]

items.title: U.S. producer inflation accelerates sharply
items.summary: The producer price index rose 1.3% in September from August and increased 6.3% year over year, up from 5.6% in August and marking the largest annual increase since December 2022. The data reinforced concerns that persistent inflation could limit the Fed’s ability to ease policy.[5][10]

items.title: Nvidia CEO seeks to calm concerns about AI financing risks
items.summary: Investor sentiment improved after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the financial strength of AI infrastructure provider CoreWeave. His comments helped ease concerns about debt-backed financing arrangements involving chip suppliers and cloud-computing companies.[2]

items.title: Indonesia faces potential downgrade from emerging-market status
items.summary: Indonesia’s stock market plunged after MSCI warned it could downgrade the country from emerging-market status, raising concerns about potential capital outflows. Broader world markets were mostly higher after the previous day’s technology-led sell-off.[6]

items.title: Regional-bank earnings and economic data in focus
items.summary: Investors were watching earnings from Travelers and regional banks including Truist, along with eurozone inflation and U.S. industrial-production data. The releases were expected to influence views on inflation, credit conditions, and the outlook for central-bank policy.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly falls below $80,000 amid broad crypto liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 for the first time in about a month before recovering near $81,600. Roughly $932 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with long positions accounting for most of the losses.[1][10]
items.source: CoinDesk via CryptoVank and Coin Edition

items.title: Crypto funds record major Bitcoin and Ether outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds saw net outflows equivalent to about 3,209 BTC, while Ether funds lost roughly 38,915 ETH in one day, adding pressure to the market rebound.[1]

items.title: Russia plans to prohibit direct peer-to-peer crypto trades
items.summary: Russia is preparing rules that would make direct peer-to-peer cryptocurrency trades unlawful from July 2027; separate restrictions already prohibit transfers from digital accounts to self-custody wallets.[2]

items.title: EU regulators classify Circle’s USDC as a significant e-money token
items.summary: The European Banking Authority classified USDC as the EU’s first significant electronic money token under MiCA, with dual oversight expected to begin in November.[1]

items.title: Richard Heart reportedly arrested in Istanbul
items.summary: Turkish media reported the arrest of Richard Schueler, founder of HEX and PulseChain, on the basis of a Finnish Red Notice. HEX fell about 30%, erasing an estimated $160 million in market value.[1][2]

items.title: Starknet community votes on independent Layer 1 research
items.summary: Starknet opened a seven-day vote allowing STRK stakers and delegators to weigh an independent Layer 1 research initiative, though any move away from Ethereum settlement would require a separate governance decision.[2]

items.title: Three Japanese banks complete yen stablecoin payment pilot
items.summary: Three Japanese banks reportedly completed a pilot testing a yen-denominated stablecoin for cross-border payments, highlighting continued institutional experimentation with blockchain settlement.[3]

items.title: Ledger announces Android-based Ledger Atom device
items.summary: Ledger announced Ledger Atom, an Android-based device designed to combine everyday applications with a dedicated crypto-security mode and an AI assistant, with release planned for mid-2027.[4]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open open-weight AI model
items.summary: Meta unveiled Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 42 billion active parameters and a 1-million-token context window. The model is positioned for coding and agentic workloads, though local deployment reportedly requires exceptionally powerful hardware.

items.title: Google expands access to Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to broader consumer, developer, and enterprise access through its apps and API. The model is marketed for complex coding, finance, legal, science, and physical-reasoning tasks, with API pricing expected to increase in December.

items.title: NVIDIA launches Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter open model aimed at enterprise AI agents and multimodal workloads. The company says it outperforms frontier models on specialized benchmarks.

items.title: Microsoft unveils MAI-Base-2 foundation model
items.summary: Microsoft introduced MAI-Base-2, a mixture-of-experts model with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 80 billion active parameters. Microsoft claims substantially improved pretraining efficiency compared with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports advances in automated mathematics
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s AlphaProof Nexus reportedly resolved nine open Erdős problems and proved dozens of mathematical conjectures using Lean-based automated proof generation. The results highlight growing AI capability in formal mathematical reasoning.

items.title: Tencent open-sources Hy Memory 2.0 agent framework
items.summary: Tencent Hunyuan released Hy Memory 2.0, including an SDK, a local memory application, and a memory-writer model designed to improve persistent memory in AI agents. The model is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

items.title: China proposes expanded AI export controls
items.summary: Chinese ministries issued a draft proposal to add 23 AI-related technologies—including large models, agents, chip designs, and computing clusters—to a national export-control list. The proposal forms part of a broader plan covering several strategic technology sectors.

items.title: Research finds human review can erase AI coding productivity gains
items.summary: A study summarized by TechRepublic reports that AI increased code production by about 30%, but delays from human review reduced or eliminated the overall productivity benefit. The findings underscore the operational limits of AI-assisted software development.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox announces Xbox Labs for browser-based gaming
items.summary: Microsoft introduced Xbox Labs, a small engineering unit exploring ways to make older-generation games playable in web browsers and distribute games across more devices.

items.title: CD Projekt Red advances original IP Project Hadar
items.summary: CD Projekt Red said it has completed the worldbuilding phase for Project Hadar, its first original intellectual property, and moved the project into development.

items.title: Console hardware sales reportedly decline sharply
items.summary: Circana data cited in industry coverage indicates Xbox hardware sales fell 33% year over year and PlayStation sales declined 25%, contributing to concern about the current console market.

items.title: Epic Games previews redesigned Epic Games Store launcher
items.summary: Epic Games reportedly opened testing for a substantially redesigned Epic Games Store launcher on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

items.title: Rockstar releases Grand Theft Auto VI launch trailer
items.summary: Rockstar Games presented a launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, which is scheduled for release on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5 on November 19, 2026, with a PC version expected later.

items.title: Nintendo showcases The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
items.summary: Nintendo released an overview trailer for its Ocarina of Time remake and showed additional material ahead of the planned November 5, 2026 release.

items.title: EA announces Battlefield 6: Game of the Year Edition
items.summary: Electronic Arts announced a Game of the Year Edition for Battlefield 6 as the shooter entered its second year and began its fifth content season.

items.title: SEGA pulls Total War: SHOGUN 2 remaster after poor reception
items.summary: SEGA acknowledged the remaster’s failed launch and removed the Total War: SHOGUN 2 remaster from sale, according to gaming-industry coverage.
